title: Timber Shelter
challenge: Connect framing, enclosure and supported seams within a finite stock pool.
change: Allocated braces and revised backing are represented in the saved building; loads from covering parts transfer to framing.
finding: One inventory supplies a hierarchy of parts, rather than one repeated component.
cover_note: Atmosphere study; inspect the saved allocated model below for exact geometry.
assumptions: Four fixed post bases; declared simple bearings and fork restraints; three allocated braces. Foundation, fasteners and physical joint capacity remain unverified.
request: Design a small public-exhibition timber shelter in Seattle, using the recorded reclaimed stock. Keep the interior free of columns.
dialogue: USER
Design a small public-exhibition timber shelter in Seattle. Use the recorded reclaimed stock; keep the interior free of columns.
AGENT
The saved brief identifies Seattle and the 2021 Seattle Building Code. A specific site, exposure and permit scope still need confirmation; today's weather is not a design load.
USER
Allow cutting and supported jointing. Include the approved visible braces and backing in the material ledger.
AGENT
Saved result: 155 installed parts from 87 source bars. Review the saved load cases and critical backing response separately from connection capacity.

title: Contour Bench
use: A continuous seat for resting and gathering
challenge: Retain the changing contour while fitting the complete demand to real stock quantities.
change: 38.1 × 88.9 mm sections and 76.2 mm station pitch replace the thin prototype family; all 716 strip IDs are retained.
finding: The stock section changes the repeating pitch and therefore the overall length.
cover_note: AI-assisted atmosphere render / inspect saved geometry inside
assumptions: R03: four terminal groups use three non-collinear idealized ties; other groups retain their recorded connections. Six unanchored levelling pads. Fastener capacity and bearing friction are unverified. R02 remains mechanism-diagnosis history.
request: Keep the approved changing-contour bench. Use straight overlapping strips and allocate the complete bench from the independent inventory snapshot.
dialogue: USER
Keep the approved contour. Use straight strips with direct overlap; do not replace them with curved plywood ribs.
AGENT
The thin-section stock cannot cover the full demand in the saved bounded pattern menu. A 38.1 × 88.9 mm family is available; section and spacing must change together.
USER
Approve the full-stock version and the 125 mm computational minimum. Preserve the accepted local prototype.
AGENT
Saved result: 716 strips, one shared stock ledger. Compare self-weight, central TOTAL 1 kN and eccentric TOTAL 1 kN under the accepted R03 connections.

title: Open Pavilion
challenge: Keep architectural scale and the open pavilion character while coordinating sections, spans and subdivisions.
change: The stock-adapted working layout retains repeated gable frames; angled-end allowances are included in cutting blanks.
finding: Inventory informs architectural dimensions before allocation checks the selected layout.
cover_note: AI-assisted atmosphere render / inspect saved geometry inside
assumptions: R02 pinned-cleat connection model and six conceptually anchored pinned foundations. Wind cases require unverified anchorage; roof covering, foundation design and joint capacity are unresolved.
request: Adapt the reference open pavilion to the complete stock snapshot. Preserve gable form and useful architectural scale; coordinate dimensions and sections.
dialogue: USER
Use the pavilion as a design reference. Keep the open sides and gable roof, but adapt dimensions and framing to the full inventory.
AGENT
This is an independent inventory scenario, not Case 2 leftovers. Coordinate spans, sections and subdivisions; include angled-cut blank allowances.
USER
Preserve architectural scale and trace every installed member back to real stock. Use explicit connections, supports and load assumptions.
AGENT
Saved result: 98 installed members. The preliminary wind response requires anchorage assumptions; site-specific compliance and physical anchor capacity remain unresolved.
